added_failures_note: the reviewed run armed no suite (manifest tests: none, receipt baseline_suite and after_suite are both null), so no arm exists from which to derive an added-failure delta; the count is zero by that absence rather than by a green pair. Its one guard, check_units.py, was run by hand and both its runs are on disk: units.log (UNIT CHECK OK) and units-negative.log (the same check failing on a planted 0.7357 ms for 735.7 ms).

findings.detail: The sentence was written in revision 7af8aff12 and left unchanged by 6bd899229, which corrected the warm step from seconds to milliseconds but not this line, so a stale figure sits beside a corrected table. check_units.py passes it because it parses only `N ms`, never `N s`. A reader quoting the headline gets both a wrong cold total and a wrong compile share.
findings.summary: The summary's cold decomposition states the three programs compile cold in 29.0 s of which 21.7 s is XLA compile, while the document's own total row (line 31) records XLA compile 28.996 s and trace 3.983 + lowering 1.240 on top of it (34.2 s), and line 33 calls XLA 79 % of the cold wall where 28.996/34.2 is 84.7 %; no receipt in logs/h200c/stages.json or any other arm contains 21.7 s.

findings.detail: Line 118 repeats the containment ('of which the topology read is 107.8 ms') and line 120 then calls the read 'outside the map', contradicting line 113 in the same section. The '~58 ms of roots, booking and contractions' split (166.2 - 107.8) and the 857.5 ms counterfactual therefore subtract one function's time from another's, and the trace section's own measurement of the map's internal contour tree (37.1 ms of 139.3 ms device time) is the figure that actually applies.
findings.summary: 'The map carries the read inside it ... the 166.2 ms map contains this read's 107.8 ms' is contradicted by the code: program.map_moments calls kernel.read (scripts/prototypes/fast_map_production/program.py:203 -> kernel.py:330), a separate fixed-shape read, and the solver calls nova.equilibrium.topology.read on its own (scripts/prototypes/fast_map_production/solver.py:237), so the two stages are disjoint and the map contains none of the measured 107.8 ms.

findings.detail: The fragment discloses all three under 'What this run did not measure', so the record is honest, but the done_when's first clause asks for the empty-store arm and the converged solve and its second asks for the whole step at batch width 16; only the map was measured at width 16 (logs/h200h/stages.json step 16). A follow-up node that measures the production solve end to end, cold and warm, would close both.
findings.summary: Two clauses the done_when names are not measured: the cold arm's operand store was warm in every arm (logs/h200c/stages.json records operand_load_seconds 0.690 with hit true, not an empty store), and the converged solve's own wall is absent, as is the production route's end-to-end wall.

findings.detail: The regex r'([0-9][0-9,]*(?:\.[0-9]+)?)\s?ms\b' never matches '29.0 s', '21.7 s' or the cold table's per-program seconds, which is exactly the class of slip the check was built for after the earlier seconds-as-milliseconds error. It is also not collected by pytest and reads its receipts from a run directory outside the repository, so it cannot run in CI; units.log and units-negative.log show it does bite on ms.
findings.summary: The guard parses only milliseconds, so every second-valued statement in the fragment is unchecked, and the one wrong number the fragment carries is a seconds statement (line 21).

findings.detail: It duplicates the capability while extending what that module lacks (first execute, executable bytes, warm median). Either the prototype should import the owner for its cold split or the owner should grow the added stages so one module holds the instrument; as landed, a later change to cold-compile attribution has two places to change.
findings.summary: cold_stages re-implements the cold compile split the repository already owns at scripts/prototypes/compile_pass_profile/profile.py:85-102 (trace_seconds, lower_seconds, compile_seconds) rather than importing or extending it, which is also the reuse target the reviewed brief named.

findings.detail: The same paragraph's line 24 reports both parts correctly (carrier 0.652 s, jet matrix 0.181 s), so the summary's single figure drops the 0.65 s carrier load from the store cost a reader is asked to accept.
findings.summary: 'the operand store loaded in 0.18 s' understates the receipt: operand_load_seconds is 0.690 s in logs/h200c/stages.json and 0.649 s in logs/h200h/stages.json, and 0.18 s is the jet matrix alone.

findings.detail: A record that names an unresolvable revision cannot be tied to the code it reviewed; this review read the resolved base, and the promoted row should carry that one.
findings.summary: orientation_base_sha records f41ee6ee18f8ae4e3ebf9e64ae7fbaeee186a5f2e, which resolves to no object; the commit the work was based on is f41ee6ee18f8ae4f3bf9e64ae7fbaeee186a5f2e.
